Pen-tailed treeshrews (Ptilocercus lowii) inhabit the lowland and montane forests of Southeast Asia, where they exhibit a suite of physiological and life-history traits that are unusual among small-bodied eutherians. The period of suckling is consequently a time of rapid but controlled growth.
